newsitem.title: GABON: Gabon's president in fresh Brazzaville peace bid.
newsitem.headline: Gabon's president in fresh Brazzaville peace bid.

text.p: Gabon's veteran president Omar Bongo has begun a fresh bid to persuade the Congo Republic's warring parties to end a showdown which has killed hundreds of people in their capital Brazzaville.

Officials said that Bongo, who proposed a truce which seems to have taken hold in Brazzaville, had met representatives of President Pascal Lissouba and his rival and predecessor, former military leader Denis Sassou Nguesso on Friday.
Bongo also met members of a national mediation committee.
"We heard what all sides had to say, how they see the situation," U.N. and Organisation of African Unity special envoy Mohamed Sahnoun, who has been mediating with Bongo, told reporters afterwards.
"There were suggestions both on consolidating the ceasefire and on what steps to take at a political level to promote national reconciliation," he said.
Fresh talks were planned on Saturday, possibly with all sides meeting together, sources close to the talks said.

The conflict began in the capital of the oil-producing former French colony after soldiers surrounded Sassou's home as part of a crackdown on private militia ahead of a now postponed July 27 presidential election.

Sahnoun has said the aim of talks is to enable a presidential election to be held within two months. Plans for a U.N.-sponsored mainly African peace force are also taking shape but similar talks in Libreville in June collapsed.
Lissouba wants a 90-day extension of his mandate, which expires at the ends of August. Sassou wants a national salvation government to run the country to elections.
A fragile truce took effect on Monday.

Shooting broke out in Brazzaville on Wednesday night but state radio there reported that rival fighters had met to bury the hatchet -- suggesting a celebration of peace progress. State television later showed the two sides fraternising.

Residents in Brazzaville said on Thursday that fighters from both sides, who have indulged in ethnic score-settling, were looting in areas under their control -- with hitherto untouched administrative buildings a target.

Brazzaville mayor Bernard Kolelas, whose militia were in the thick of political and ethnic clashes that killed at least 2,000 people after a disputed 1993 parliamentary election, heads the national mediation committee.
He, Lissouba and Sassou were all due to contest the July 27 poll. Lissouba defeated Kolelas in the run-off of a first multi-party election 1992.
All three rivals were in Brazzaville on Friday.
